summary.short: CRU decision, published 12 December 2025, directing Irish electricity system operators on grid connection of data centres. Data centres at or above 1 MVA must supply matching dispatchable or autoproducer generation, meet 80% of annual demand with Irish renewable electricity within a six-year glide path, and self-report annually.
summary.long: Decision paper CRU/2025/236 of the Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU), published 12 December 2025, sets the connection policy for large electricity demand. It applies exclusively to data centres seeking connection to the electricity network and sets a de minimis level of 1 MVA below which its elements do not apply. Data centres at or above 1 MVA and below 10 MVA must provide an autoproducer unit in the Single Electricity Market meeting 100% of their maximum import capacity on a de-rated basis. Those at or above 10 MVA must provide separately connected dispatchable onsite or proximate generation or storage matching their capacity. Both must meet at least 80% of annual demand with renewable electricity generated in Ireland, with a six-year glide path from energisation. A connection cannot ramp up without the associated generation in place. Compliant data centres are not subject to Mandatory Demand Curtailment. System operators must publish locational information and a connection process by 31 March 2026, and data centres self-report annually. A Section 34 direction to the system operators supersedes CRU/21/124 for new applications; applications already in process continue under that direction. Gas connection rules are not changed. Non-compliance may lead to a reduction in the maximum import capacity.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the paper from the summary to section 3.5.7 (Compliance with requirements). The System Operator direction (section 6.2), sections 7 and 8 and Appendix A are in part 2 and are not annotated here. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry IDs were supplied for the cited Acts, Regulations, Directives or CRU papers. Internal points: the proposed de-minimis level was 500kW or 1MW (section 2.2) and the decision sets 1 MVA; this is a change from the proposal, not an internal conflict. Section 3.3 heading reads 'de-minims (1 MVA)' (typo). The 80% renewable requirement is stated as annual with a 6-year glide path from energisation (3.5.5 to 3.5.7). Section 3.1.3 says the renewable requirement rests on section 9(1)(s) of the 1999 Act, not the Climate Action Act. Section 3.1.3 states the Supreme Court decision in the Coolglass appeal was awaited when the paper was written. Binding effect of the requirements depends on the direction and contractual terms described in part 2. Part 2 covers sections 3.6 to 3.9, 4 to 8 and Appendix A. Inconsistencies: section 3.6.6 gives the amending act for Article 50 of Regulation (EU) 2019/943 as 2024/1747 and the directive amending Directive (EU) 2019/944 as 2024/1711, while section 3.9.3 gives 2024/1711 and 2024/1771 respectively. Section 8 says Direction CRU/21/124 is superseded, but section 3.9.6 says applications received before publication continue under CRU/21/124. Table 6 (section 3.9.7) is garbled in the extracted text, so the scenario-to-approach mapping is not reliably readable. Respondent names and views in Appendix A are not annotated. Climate Act references in Appendix A and section 7.1.2 are respondent feedback as summarised by the CRU.

obligations.summary: Data centre connection applicants must provide dispatchable and renewable generation; for MIC of at least 1MVA and under 10MVA, an autoproducer unit meeting 100% of MIC (de-rated); for MIC of 10MVA or above, new onsite or proximate dispatchable generation and/or storage equal to or greater than MIC (de-rated), separately connected and metered; applications are also assessed on location as constrained or unconstrained.
obligations.applies_from: Applies to new connection applications following publication of the decision
obligations.conditional_on: MIC at or above the de-minimis level of 1MVA; tiers at 1MVA to under 10MVA and at 10MVA or above

evidence.provision: Section 6.2.1 New Direction to the System Operators
evidence.quote: to provide an autoproducer unit in the wholesale electricity market which meets 100% of the demand sites MIC

obligations.summary: Data centre applicants with MIC at or above the de-minimis level must meet at least 80% of annual demand through additional renewable electricity generated in the Republic of Ireland, and demonstrate a credible plan for this, within a 6-year period from energisation of the demand site.
obligations.applies_from: Within a 6-year period from the date of the demand site's energisation
obligations.conditional_on: MIC at or above the de-minimis level of 1MVA

evidence.provision: Section 6.2.1 New Direction to the System Operators
evidence.quote: Applicants will be required to demonstrate a credible plan in relation to how they intend to meet these requirements within a 6-year period

obligations.summary: System Operators (EirGrid as TSO and ESBN as DSO) must assess data centre connection applications by reference to the stated assessment criteria, and the application terminates where the SO is not satisfied that an offer can be made.
obligations.applies_from: Applies to new connection applications following publication of the decision

evidence.provision: Section 6.2.1 New Direction to the System Operators
evidence.quote: the CRU directs EirGrid (as TSO) & ESBN (as DSO) to assess applications for the connection of data centres

obligations.summary: Where the SO refuses to offer a connection agreement, it must provide the applicant with the reasons for the refusal; Section 3.9.4 adds that where refusal is due to lack of network capacity, the SO must provide information on reinforcement measures.
obligations.applies_from: Applies to new connection applications following publication of the decision

evidence.provision: Section 6.2.1 New Direction to the System Operators
evidence.quote: Where the SO refuses to offer into a connection agreement, they shall provide the applicant with the reasons for the refusal.

obligations.summary: System Operators must update the relevant contractual requirements needed to enforce the decisions in the paper.

evidence.quote: Update the relevant contractual requirements required to enforce the decisions set out on this paper.

obligations.summary: System Operators must provide a bi-annual report to the CRU on the implementation and effectiveness of the policy.

evidence.quote: Provide a bi-annual report to the CRU on the implementation and effectiveness of this policy.

obligations.summary: Energy assets required under the policy must meet the same performance and availability requirements as other equivalent units in the system, with reliability of service a contractual requirement; the SOs may reduce the MIC or move the connection to non-firm status if minimum reliability is not met.
obligations.conditional_on: Energy assets required under the policy

evidence.quote: the energy assets required under this policy should have to meet the same performance and availability requirements as any other equivalent unit in the system

enforcement.triggered_by: Delivery, performance or availability of the onsite or proximate generation and/or storage falls below the minimum expected reliability set by the SOs
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Reduction of the MIC of the related data centre's demand connection; no monetary penalty stated in this part

evidence.quote: the SOs will have the ability to reduce the MIC of the related data centre’s demand connection.

enforcement.triggered_by: Data centre fails to meet the minimum 80% renewable electricity generated in the Republic of Ireland requirement following the end of the 6-year glide path
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Reduction of the MIC of the related data centre's demand connection to the level met successfully by 80% renewable electricity; no monetary penalty stated in this part
enforcement.cure_period: 6-year glide path from the date of the demand site's energisation

evidence.quote: the SOs will have the ability to reduce the MIC of the related data centre’s demand connection to the level met successfully by 80% renewable electricity.

enforcement.triggered_by: Breach of the requirements associated with the connection policy, as reflected in contracts between the SOs and connection applicants

evidence.quote: Any breach of the requirements could result in actions up to and including a termination of the connection agreement.

enforcement.triggered_by: Delivery, performance or availability of required energy services falling below the minimum expected reliability, or below the provision of available capacity to the system
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Not stated in this text; the consequence is a reduction of the MIC of the related data centre demand connection and/or move to non-firm status

evidence.quote: the SOs will have the ability to reduce the MIC of the related data centres demand connection and/or move it to non-firm status.

enforcement.authority: ESB Networks (under its Flexible Demand Connections Initiative, as described in the text)
enforcement.triggered_by: Customer failing to comply with instructions to reduce consumption when accepting a flexible connection
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Not stated in this text; the text says failure to comply could result in disconnection

evidence.quote: As part of the conditions when accepting a flexible connection, a customer must comply with instructions to reduce consumption, failure to do so could result in disconnection.
